Rashi on Nedarim 49a:10:1.english: [The] sick [are] the Sages - For they engage in Torah and do not enjoy [the pleasures of] the world, and [thus] come to sickness.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:1:1.hebrew: הנודר מן המבושל מותר בצלי ובשלוק - מבושל, מבושל כראוי:
Rashi on Nedarim 49a:1:1.english: One who vows [to abstain] from cooked [food] is permitted roasted and boiled [food] - "Cooked" [means] properly cooked.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:1:3.english: Konam, a cooked dish that I will not taste - Any cooked dish is implied.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:1:4.english: A loose dish cooked in a pot - That has broth in it.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:1:5.english: But not [from] a thick [one] - Such as porridge.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:1:6.english: Turemuta, the remutza - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:1:7.hebrew: רתחתא - דבר הרותח, כגון רוטב וכל דדמי ליה:
Rashi on Nedarim 49a:1:7.english: Retachta [boiling] - Something that boils, such as broth and anything similar to it.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:1:8.english: That which goes down into a pot - For it implies both cold and hot.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:1:9.english: [He is] prohibited from [tasting] anything cooked - whether loose or thick.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:2:1.hebrew: ר' יאשיה אוסר - בצלי ובשלוק, דמתקרי נמי מבושל:
Rashi on Nedarim 49a:2:1.english: Rabbi Yoshiya prohibits - roasted and overcooked [food], for it is also called "cooked."

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:3:1.english: Follow the language of people - For it is not their custom to call roasted [food] "cooked".

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:6:1.english: But didn't he vow [against] cooked food - For [it] implies both soft and thick.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:7:1.hebrew: האי תנא - דמתניתין, דלא קרי לעבה תבשיל:
Rashi on Nedarim 49a:7:1.english: This tanna - [the tanna] of our Mishnah, who does not call a thick [dish] a cooked food.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:7:2.english: With anything with which bread is eaten - [That] with which they accompany the bread is called a cooked dish.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:7:3.english: And it is taught - [This is said] calmly [i.e., as a statement rather than an objection].

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:7:4.english: From soft hiteriyyot - [That is,] soft gourds with which the sick eat their bread.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:8:1.english: Is that so? - Do the sick eat from them [gourds]?

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:8:2.english: He saw a gourd that was placed - A gourd placed there, from which he was eating.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:9:1.english: The innards of the gourd with chard - The inside of a gourd is good to eat with chard.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:9:2.english: The inner part of flax - The inner part of flax seeds [is] good to eat with kutach.

Rashi on Nedarim 49a:9:3.hebrew: ודבר זה אסור לאומרו בפני עם הארץ - משום דדבר מעולה הוא לרפואה, ואסור לומר להם שום דבר שיהנו ממנו. ואית דאמרי: דלא ליכלו טובא וליפסדו כיתנא:
Rashi on Nedarim 49a:9:3.english: And this matter is forbidden to be said in the presence of an ignoramus - Because it is a superior thing for healing, and it is forbidden to tell them anything from which they would benefit. And some say: [It is] so that they do not eat a lot [of it] and ruin the flax.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:10:1.english: Who are the sick - [That] which [the baraita] taught above: "that the sick eat," etc.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:10:2.hebrew: רבנן - שמתוך שעמלים בתורה הם חלשים, אבל לחולין ממש לא מעלי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:10:2.english: The Sages - Because they toil in Torah, they are weak, whereas for those who are actually sick, [a gourd] is not beneficial.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:10:3.english: Rava [conforms] to his [own] reasoning - That the Sages are called sick.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:1:1.english: "One who vows [that] cooked [food is forbidden] is permitted [to eat] roasted and shaluk [food]" - Shaluk [refers to food] that is not cooked further [i.e., it is only partially cooked].

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:1:2.hebrew: קונם תבשיל שאני טועם אסור במעשה קדירה רך - מפרש בגמרא: כל מידי שנותנין בו פת לשרות קרוי תבשיל, ומותר בעבה שאינו נאכל עם פת. וצ"ע אמאי שני למיתני ענין אחר מרישא: לפלוג בנודר מן התבשיל בלא שאומר "שאני טועם", ובשאר בבי — כבוש ושלוק ומליח — נקט דווקא "שאני טועם" להוסיף בו איסור! וי"ל: רבותא נקטי', דאפ"ה מותר בעבה; וברישא מצי למיתני "מבושל שאני טועם מותר בצלי ובשלוק", אלא לא היה תופס חידוש [בהאי], דמבושל לא משמע בשום ייתור צלי ושלוק:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:1:2.english: "[Cooked food is] konam, that I will not taste [it], he is prohibited from a loose dish cooked in a pot" - It is explained in the Gemara: anything into which one puts bread to soak is called tavshil (cooked food), and he is permitted [to eat] a thick [dish], since it is not eaten with bread. And this requires further study: why did [the Mishnah] change to teach a different formulation from the first clause? It should have made the distinction in [the case of] one who vows from tavshil without saying "that I will not taste," whereas in the other clauses — pickled, boiled, and salted — it specifically used "that I will not taste" to add prohibition to it! And one can answer: it states a novel point, that even so he is permitted [to eat] a thick [dish]; and in the first clause [the Mishnah] could have taught "[Mevushal] that I will not taste — he is permitted roasted and boiled," except that it would not have conveyed a novelty in this [case], because mevushal does not imply roasted or boiled even with any extra phrasing.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:1:3.english: [Turemuta and remutza] - [It is] explained in the Gemara:

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:2:1.hebrew: רבי יאשיה אוסר בצלי, ואע"פ שאין ראיה לדבר — זכר לדבר - ולכך לא הוי ראיה, דבנדרים הלך אחר לשון בני אדם:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:2:1.english: "Rabbi Yoshiya prohibits roasted [food], and although there is no proof of the matter — [there is] an allusion to the matter." - And therefore it is not a [conclusive] proof, because regarding vows, follow the common parlance of people.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:6:1.hebrew: והא מן תבשיל נדר - ורך לא הוי תבשיל, כיון שהוא רק כמים בעלמא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:6:1.english: But didn’t he vow from a cooked dish - And a loose [dish] is not [considered] a cooked dish, since it is merely like water.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:8:1.hebrew: [איני] - וכי קרי טובים לחולים וכו':
Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:8:1.english: [Is that so] - Are gourds good for the sick, etc.?

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:9:1.english: With soft [gourds] - [they] are beneficial to the sick.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:9:2.hebrew: באשוני - פירוש: קשות, הם רעות לחולה, שאינן מבושלות כצורך:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:9:2.english: Be'ashunei [to hard ones] - Explanation: hard [gourds]; they are bad for a sick person, as they are not cooked as needed.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:9:3.hebrew: בקרא גופה - פירוש: חיצון שבקרא קשה הוא ורע לחולה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:9:3.english: To the gourd itself - Explanation: The outer part of the gourd is hard and bad for a sick person.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:9:4.english: In its interior - The soft [part] inside it is beneficial for a sick person.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:9:5.english: Luliva dekara [The innards of the gourd] - Anything that is [soft] is called luliva.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:9:6.english: With kutach - [It is] good to put [it] in kutach.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:9:7.hebrew: ודבר זה אסור לאומרו בפניהם - שמלעיגים עלינו ואומרין שאנו קובעים מילי דחוכא ואיטלולא בהש"ס, ובקונט' פירש שאסור ללמוד להם שום תקנה, ולא נראה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49a:9:7.english: And this matter is forbidden to say in their presence - for they mock us and say that we establish matters of jest and mockery in the Talmud. And in the Kuntres [Rashi], he explained that it is forbidden to teach them any remedy, but [this] does not appear [correct].
